- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter to reduce overshoot by 10–20% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); cap forecast tail end at 1.5–2.0σ above recent 10-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model tends to lag; adjust forecast by +0.5–1.0% for each prior sentiment reversal in last 5 days.
